<color=#ffd780>About the Hexenzirkel</color>
The "guide who will never get lost" is N, otherwise known as Nicole. You may have not encountered her yet, but she is a truly extraordinary woman who has made this world's direction and order her subject of study.
Some of you may be fortunate enough to have already heard her voice. Like a prophetess, she will only speak to guide people toward the truth when a change has occurred in the world.
She has a tendency to... suddenly speak in someone's mind without any warning.
If one day, you would be unfortunate enough to run into a truly dangerous situation, she may use her voice to guide the way forward for you.

customize.name: Columbina
customize.desc: The Moon Maiden born in Nod-Krai, and also the welkin moon returning home.

customize.text: Character Story

<color=#ffd680>Character Story 4</color>
On nights when the moon was full, Columbina liked to quietly leave the Silvermoon Hall and wander near the homes of the little animals. Sometimes it would be a tree hollow, at others a bird's nest. She would stand nearby, listening to the steady rhythm of their breaths while lifting her eyes to the moon above. It was as if, by doing so, she could imagine what nighttime on the moon might be like — quiet and peaceful. She hoped it was.
On nights like these, she pieced together dreams of what a "home" might be.
When she once again returned to Hiisi Island, she met a certain contemporary Moonchanter. Columbina had spent much time with the Frostmoon Scions, yet she had never once seen such beautiful, enormous antlers.
"...Forgive my interruption," Canon, the goddess of the Frost Moon, interrupted. "I thought there were quite a few with antlers among the Frostmoon Scions."
Columbina explained that while it had been historically common, few were born with antlers today, and none boasted antlers as splendid as that Moonchanter's.
"The bloodline inevitably grew diluted, I see..." The Frost Moon goddess sighed. "Sorry... Please continue, Columbina Hyposelenia."
After meeting that Moonchanter, Columbina occasionally made surreptitious visits to her home as well. She discovered, however, that the moon's tides seemed to bring some restless pain to said Moonchanter. In those moments, Columbina would try to use her own power to soothe the tides surrounding the woman. Sometimes, she would find herself humming familiar melodies, instinctively — the lullaby that had once comforted her before her birth.
"A lullaby from before your birth?" This time it was Aria, goddess of the Eternal Moon, who spoke up.
Columbina explained the melodies she had heard before being born.
The three goddesses shook their heads. They had no knowledge of this song.
Columbina continued to tell them stories of the future world: From the flavors of offerings in that world, to the music in its opera houses... From a friend with a clockwork mechanism in her back, to a former angel who became her friend...
Finally, she spoke of the Moon-Prayer Night.
The three moon goddesses were deeply moved by the beauty of that evening — perhaps also because Columbina herself could not help but smile as she recounted it.
"In our time, the gods of the heavens rarely had such profound connections with the world below," the goddess of the Frost Moon said.
"Yes. Everyone was nice to me. We even played water-ball games together."
"Unimaginable. It seems our era was far too conservative," the goddess of the Eternal Moon said, clearly astonished.
"We even stuck little stickers on each other's faces."
A few soft gasps of surprise came from the three goddesses.
"We also exchanged food, tasting the candy in each other's hands."
The goddesses fell silent. Columbina felt glances tinted with envy pass between them.
Long moments passed. Then Sonnet, goddess of the Iridescent Moon, finally breathed a sigh of amazement.
"Wow..."

She sent a whole lot and even gave me detailed explanations about the inspiration and setting for each one. I asked her when I might be able to read a book she had authored herself, but then I suddenly stopped hearing from her. Perhaps... she went off to write one.

customize.name: Durin
customize.desc: A dragon born from M's pen, who came to alight in the human world. His "story" continues to unfold.

customize.text: Character Story

<color=#ffd680>Character Story 5</color>
Carried by the wind that Venti had gifted him, Durin caught up with Dvalin, soaring together into the skies above Windrise. And finally, the story the mage had been writing arrived at the chapter she had been waiting for.
Standing by the long table where mages gathered for meetings, Alice watched Durin's figure recede into the distance. Her thoughts drifted back through the years to a tea party where all seven of them had been present. Delighted by the occasion, she had been struck by a whim to start a story-telling game, only to stumble when choosing a theme. She turned to Anya, the writer among them, who offered a simple, potent answer: "The Undying Fire."
"If I ever get the chance, I want to leave behind an 'Undying Fire' through my stories. As an author, that is the greatest pursuit I can imagine."
"An 'Undying Fire'? What exactly does that mean?"
"I suspect each of us has our own answer to that question. Isn't that what makes it perfect for a storytelling relay? I am still searching for my own answer, in any case."
Anya didn't answer directly. As she often did in her own works, she left a hint of suspense, sparking Alice's curiosity.
"All right, then, let's go with this theme! Each time we meet, the next person will take their turn and write their chapter. Hmm... Anya, you take the final chapter. By the time the story reaches its conclusion, I expect you'll have your answer ready for me."
And so began the relay. Alice volunteered to write the opening — the little witch set off on a journey to find the "Undying Fire" in order to complete the trials set by the old witch.
What Alice didn't anticipate was that by the time the witches gathered again, Anya had passed away, lying in her coffin, asleep forever. She had misjudged how differently witches and humans experienced the passage of time, and how profoundly that would affect Anya. She had been expecting to wait for the next chapter, but Anya had already grown old. By the time the story reached the fifth volume, Anya was gone.
The tale Alice had begun started veering wildly in the second and third volumes, handled as they were by Barbeloth and Rhinedottir respectively, but it was partially rescued in the fourth volume under Ivanovna. Yet in the fifth volume, penned by Nicole, it was hastily concluded in a single line. Alice felt frustrated, convinced she would never learn the answer Anya had intended.
The story took a turn with Octavia. The Hexenzirkel had never been marred by a loss since its founding until Anya's passing, a loss that now brought the frequently-absent Octavia to the gathering. She brought with her the already written sixth volume, in which the little witch was given a second chance, reuniting with the old witch.
"The Undying Fire might exist after all," she said.
In response to Octavia's reminder, Alice turned her attention to the final work Anya had left behind — the world they had created together, Simulanka. In this world, a dragon named Durin waited, restless and uncertain, for miracles that might come in the future. The possibilities Anya had woven into him, much like the unresolved threads she left in her other works, glowed like a softly burning flame, illuminating the world of the story and tugging at Alice's curiosity. Gazing at this flame, Alice recalled the promise she had once made to Anya.
"It seems the ending she was meant to write falls to my pen instead."
And so the years passed, with Alice often turning her gaze to the dragon. She watched the child, once burdened with the name of a drake most fell, receive blessings from others, step out of the world of the story, make friends, forge connections with the world beyond the tale, and together with his companions face and overcome fate. In the end, she saw him completely rewrite the story of Durin the wicked dragon and take flight alongside Dvalin...
Drawing her thoughts back, Alice realized she had finally received Anya's answer.
"Anya, just as I wrote at the end of the storytelling relay, I've always thought you were the most capable among us."
"You always say you would leave little behind, but I see it now — the undying fire you left for us."
Dialogues

<color=#ffd780>About wolves</color>
Why not wolves? Many a tale has wolves in it, and even the compendium personally burned by Madame Mage had a wolf character!
It is said that the Boar Tribe were once all wild boars, but the boars did bad things, so the master wanted to punish them.
The master took out a rusted set of scales, and told the boars to stack their own things on both sides. If the scales tipped to one side, they could leave.
But the scales were so rusty that putting just a small amount of weight was not enough to move them.
Those boars who placed their heads on the scales became wolves, lizards, and snakes, leaving only their strength. Those who offered their muscles became rabbits, leaping three paces to a bound, instinctively guiding people to treasure.
But there was one boar who placed things evenly on both sides, until the rusted scale broke right down the middle...
And so she became a mute person — for she had placed her voice upon the scales as well.
She is also a friend of Madame Mage, and I hear she likes to speak in people's heads!

desc.text:
(Messy handwriting. This doesn't seem much like a fortune slip...)
In truth, I said all I wished to say to you in the end, but Alice still advised me to write a little, saying that what I cannot say aloud, I can always write, surely. That is the case, though I have spoken directly into peoples' minds for so long... that I never practiced my penmanship anyway.
No need to worry if I've pried into any of your innermost thoughts, I've never done anything like that. If that does not reassure you, let me share one of my secrets with you. Having been suffocated by my inability to speak, I wound up being an incredibly talkative person at first. Alice noted that those who used their real mouths to blather on with had far fewer problems than I, since I would set my head abuzz and give myself quite a headache whenever I spoke. She advised me to speak more steadily and present an air of mystery and nobility — which is how I wound up speaking the way you remember.
I'm off, in any case. There's not much to worry about here with you — so why don't you watch over me instead?

<color=#ffffffd9>(Archon Quest Interlude Chapter: Act III - Inversion of Genesis, As Though Morning Dew)</color>
<color=#37ffff>Nicole</color> : You sound lost and confused.
<color=#37ffff>Paimon</color> : ...Who's that?
<color=#37ffff>Nicole</color> : I know why you are troubled. Any who knew of this would find their mind overwhelmed.
<color=#37ffff>Paimon</color> : Huh? Is there someone here talking to us?
<color=#37ffff>Nicole</color> : Unfortunately, the fate of Teyvat cannot easily be changed. Perhaps a god may have a slim chance, but for anyone else... who can say.
<color=#37ffff>Nicole</color> : When a small animal runs into a tree trunk, though the tree may sway, it is not displaced. The same is true of fate.
<color=#37ffff>Nicole</color> : Like a vase that falls to the ground. Whether it is broken by a cat or by a bird, the result is still a broken vase, is it not?
<color=#37ffff>Paimon</color> : Wh—Who are you!? How do you know about all this?
<color=#37ffff>Nicole</color> : History does not change easily, but human hearts can. Believe your own eyes. Only that which you see is true. What is unseen is but an illusion.

<color=#ffffffd9>(Archon Quest Chapter IV: Act V - Masquerade of the Guilty, Hunters, Prophets)</color>
<color=#37ffff>Paimon</color> : Uh, did you just pour some tea? Paimon didn't notice you doing that at all!
<color=#37ffff>Traveler</color> : No, I didn't.
<color=#37ffff>Paimon</color> : Th—Then what's that?
<color=#37ffff>Paimon</color> : ...Paimon's never seen that cup before!
<color=#37ffff>Nicole</color> : Don't be frightened. I'm just joining you two for tea. I merely refrained from saying anything till now.
<color=#37ffff>Paimon</color> : Ah! Who's that voice!? But there's no one here!
<color=#37ffff>Nicole</color> : Ah, have you forgotten me already?
<color=#37ffff>Paimon</color> : Wait... You *are* familiar...
<color=#37ffff>Paimon</color> : You're the voice we heard from the sky in Sumeru!
<color=#37ffff>Nicole</color> : "The voice from the sky," hmm? I fear that description is wrong — though not completely wrong.
<color=#37ffff>Nicole</color> : You're feeling lost now, just as you were feeling previously. I sensed that confusion, and thus came to you. Guiding people is an irresistible hobby of mine, after all.
<color=#37ffff>Traveler</color> : Who are you? And what do you want with us?
<color=#37ffff>Nicole</color> : Consider me a passerby, just accepting a commission from my friend's disciple on a whim.
<color=#37ffff>Traveler</color> : Allow me to ask you...
<color=#37ffff>Traveler</color> : Will Fontaine's prophecy come true?
<color=#37ffff>Nicole</color> : The prophecy... Yes, what has been prophesized will be fulfilled. You may view such things as "the history of the future."
<color=#37ffff>Paimon</color> : What... Th—Then, is there any way we can stop it?
<color=#37ffff>Nicole</color> : People call such things "fate," and it is written in the stars — it cannot so easily be altered.
<color=#37ffff>Traveler</color> : There it is again... "fate."
<color=#37ffff>Traveler</color> : Can there really be no exceptions?
<color=#37ffff>Nicole</color> : Ah, so you've caught on.
<color=#37ffff>Nicole</color> : Just as prophecies are usually only the future as seen from the perspectives of the gods, could things be happening in hidden corners where the gods' gaze does not fall?
<color=#37ffff>Nicole</color> : Are the things that you shall see different from the fate that the gods perceive?
<color=#37ffff>Paimon</color> : Wh—What is she talking about? It all sounds really impressive and important and stuff... but it also sounds kinda scary.
(The tea in the teacup is just about gone as well...)
<color=#37ffff>Nicole</color> : I believe that you understand, right? Some things are insignificant... but others, you must reach out to change.
<color=#37ffff>Nicole</color> : Ultimately, fate shall serve as your only guide no matter what will happen in Teyvat's future. All you need to do is to play your part.
<color=#37ffff>Nicole</color> : This was good tea, by the way. Thank you for your hospitality. Well, that'll be all for today.
<color=#37ffff>Paimon</color> : The voice... it's gone.
